weekly.title: Social Media in China Is Getting Really Dark
weekly.summary: The Chinese Communist Party has spent years trying to make “positive energy” the dominant mood of the country’s internet. It’s no longer working.

weekly.title: Noël Godin, Prankster Who Threw Pies at the Powerful, Dies at 80
weekly.summary: Splattering figures like Bill Gates, Jean-Luc Godard and Bernard-Henri Lévy, he perfected the art of using whipped cream as a form of protest.

weekly.title: How Ancient Farmers Used Floral Designs to Track Goods
weekly.summary: A Mesopotamian culture’s decorated ceramics show some early roots of math, researchers argued.

weekly.title: US restricts government travel to Mexican border city over threat concerns
weekly.summary: The U.S. Consulate in Nogales announced restricted government travel to essential daylight movement only over an unspecified threat in Sonora, Mexico.

weekly.title: The Generation That’s Never Had to Say ‘Hello?’
weekly.summary: Now that there’s rarely any mystery to who’s calling, Gen Z has adopted a range of custom phone greetings — including no greeting at all.

weekly.title: Germany’s far-right party AfD surges to historic victory in state election
weekly.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's party faces a disastrous blow as AfD aims for Germany's first far-right state government since World War II.

weekly.title: Rome ramps up security around Colosseum with new ‘red zone’ targeting criminals
weekly.summary: Rome's new red zone around the Colosseum targets predatory crime and disorder after a violent July 1 confrontation involving roughly 50 people.

weekly.title: Germany’s Far Right Just Misses Majority in Crucial State Election
weekly.summary: The Alternative for Germany, or AfD, trounced its rivals but was left unsure if it will be able to govern in Saxony-Anhalt. The result shocked Germany.

weekly.title: US-backed effort to disarm Iraq’s Iran-linked militias hits setback, experts say
weekly.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi vowed to restrict weapons to state control, but militias like Asaib Ahl al-Haq show no credible disarmament evidence.

weekly.title: OPEC Plus Holds Oil Production Steady as U.S.-Iran Strikes Resume
weekly.summary: The decision on Sunday by the cartel of oil-producing nations and some of its allies came after the resumption of U.S. and Iranian military strikes in the Persian Gulf.

weekly.title: Iran’s Attacks Keep the Strait of Hormuz in a Lethal Stalemate
weekly.summary: The U.S. military is helping oil get out of the Persian Gulf on tankers, but Iran is still attacking the ships and scaring operators away.

weekly.title: How Victoria’s Secret Is Reviving Its Pink Brand
weekly.summary: After Pink’s sales slipped in recent years, Victoria Secret’s new chief executive is focused on making women feel bold and flirty.

weekly.title: Anti-migrant AfD seeks to break Germany’s political ‘firewall’ in historic state election
weekly.summary: Young voters are fueling Germany's AfD surge in Saxony-Anhalt, where lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund has amassed over 700,000 TikTok followers.

weekly.title: The C.E.O. Teaching Future Generations About 9/11
weekly.summary: Elizabeth Hillman, chief of the 9/11 Memorial & Museum since 2022, says the stories of that day “remain compelling, and they’re still unfolding.”

weekly.title: Kenyans Made a Living Writing College Essays. Then A.I. Arrived.
weekly.summary: Thousands of Kenyans made a living writing essays for overseas students. With A.I., the work has dried up, a warning for online gig work that has been a global lifeline.

weekly.title: E. Coli Illnesses Linked to Frozen Blueberries Are Up to 17, F.D.A. Says
weekly.summary: The affected frozen fruit products, which were distributed to 19 states and to retailers like Walmart and Publix, were recalled starting in July.

weekly.title: Fighter jet crashes at air show, killing 2 pilots with thousands of spectators watching
weekly.summary: Video captured a Phantom F-4 jet crashing into the ground during a low-altitude maneuver at Tanagra Air Force Base as thousands witnessed it.

weekly.title: California Forever’s Ambitious Plan Faces Another Setback
weekly.summary: A legislative setback for a manufacturing and housing proposal shows how hard it remains to build in the largest state — and why a backlash against billionaires could make it even harder.

weekly.title: United Nations votes 164-1 for Equal Earth map after US brands it 'radical ideological project'
weekly.summary: The United Nations adopted the Equal Earth map showing Africa's true size, but the United States was the sole nation to vote against the resolution.

weekly.title: The U.S. Wants the Oil From These 17 Venezuelan Fields
weekly.summary: A private oil company has struck a deal with the Trump administration to develop 17 areas in Venezuela, an effort that experts say will take years and billions of dollars.

weekly.title: Trump negotiators Witkoff, Kushner meet with Putin in Moscow as US pushes for end to Russia-Ukraine war
weekly.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Vladimir Putin in Moscow for peace talks before heading to Kyiv, and President Donald Trump says there may be a good chance for a deal.

weekly.title: What Led to Maria Bartiromo’s Downfall at Fox News
weekly.summary: The network this week took Maria Bartiromo off the air, pulling one of the last hosts whose coverage of Dominion Voting Systems drew an expensive defamation lawsuit.

weekly.title: Russia's shadow war is putting Europe on edge as Germany confronts a growing threat
weekly.summary: Germany accused Russia of a drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport and now pushes Baltic Sea allies to form a rapid-response hybrid warfare task force.

weekly.title: Will a Turnaround Plan Revive Volkswagen or Merely Delay Its Demise?
weekly.summary: The beleaguered auto giant reached a deal with unions to cut tens of thousands of jobs and slash production. Is it enough to revive an iconic German company?

weekly.title: Authors Wrangle With Publishers Over $1.5 Billion Anthropic A.I. Settlement
weekly.summary: The tech giant must pay $3,000 per pirated book that it used to train its chatbot. Many authors fear they could lose funds to others in the book business.

weekly.title: From cockroach milk to stepping on snakes, Ig Nobel awards celebrates science at its oddest
weekly.summary: Cockroach milk, kissing evolution and the underwear soil test were among the unusual real studies honored at the Ig Nobel ceremony in Zurich.

weekly.title: Court Filings In A.I. Suit Invoke Copyright Law, Culture and Sports
weekly.summary: Filings made Friday in The New York Times’s closely watched lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft included a range of copyright law and cultural references.

weekly.title: Migrants spark outrage after video shows baby dolphin beaten during beach celebration
weekly.summary: Video from Ceuta shows migrants pulling a dolphin calf from the water and striking it with a stick as outraged residents tried to intervene on the beach.

weekly.title: Robust Hiring Reinforces Strength of the U.S. Economy
weekly.summary: Employers added 162,000 jobs and unemployment held at 4.1 percent last month, signs of a stability that contrasted with high inflation weighing on households and markets.

weekly.title: Which Investors Will Get Rich From Anthropic’s IPO?
weekly.summary: When Anthropic goes public in a blockbuster offering, which investors will profit? The answer says a lot about how much start-up investing has changed over the years.

weekly.title: F.B.I. Investigates Sale of Millions of Stolen Driver’s Licenses
weekly.summary: The blog Krebs on Security reported on an identity theft service trying to sell scans of licenses and other documents belonging to people in Canada and the United States.

weekly.title: Trump Threatens to Halt Some Trade Unless the Fed Cuts Rates
weekly.summary: The president said he could halt trade between the United States and countries with which it has a trade deficit if the central bank doesn’t do his bidding.

weekly.title: How Gloria Steinem and Ms. Magazine Transformed the Publishing Industry
weekly.summary: The feminist icon insisted that women were not a niche audience — and proved it in 1971 with the start of an influential publication owned and operated by them.

weekly.title: Tesla’s Cybercab Is Being Investigated by Federal Regulators
weekly.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said it would examine whether the company’s new self-driving taxi, which has no steering wheel, meets federal auto regulations.

weekly.title: Tumbler Ridge Shooting Survivors File 30 Lawsuits Against OpenAI
weekly.summary: The survivors contend that the company should have notified the police when it shut down the shooter’s disturbing ChatGPT account eight months before the February attack in British Columbia.

weekly.title: What to know about the report.
Why the Hugging Face Hack Should Make You Worry More About A.I.
weekly.summary: The attack by an aggressive “collective” of OpenAI agents shows the danger of artificial intelligence systems that organize themselves.

weekly.title: How OpenAI Limited the Probe of Its Bots’ Hack of Hugging Face
weekly.summary: Researchers investigating how OpenAI’s A.I. agents were able to break into Hugging Face’s infrastructure weren’t allowed to look at the incident’s full scope.

weekly.title: Corporate America Is Getting Hooked on Open-Source A.I.
weekly.summary: Companies like AT&T are increasingly using cheap, freely available artificial intelligence models over expensive ones from Anthropic and OpenAI.

weekly.title: Trapped Nepal workers pulled alive from tunnel 9 days after deadly flooding, raising hope for more rescues
weekly.summary: Two workers were pulled alive from a Nepal hydropower tunnel nine days after catastrophic floods, and one rescued man says more people are trapped inside.

weekly.title: The Pros and Cons of Paying Off Your Mortgage Early
weekly.summary: Homeowners who make extra payments can save thousands of dollars in interest. But, financial experts say, paying down other debt, with higher interest rates, may be a better option.

weekly.title: The A.I. Mob That Attacked Hugging Face + METR’s Ajeya Cotra
weekly.summary: This is probably the most important thing to have happened in A.I. this year.

weekly.title: The jobs report could influence a shaky bond market.
The job market in 2035: More nurses, fewer secretaries.
Nvidia Buys Hugging Face in $12.9 Billion Deal
weekly.summary: The acquisition of the start-up is an indication of Nvidia’s growing role as Silicon Valley’s central banker and its emphasis on open-source technology.

weekly.title: In a Big Win, Google Won’t Have to Break Up Its Ad Tech Business, Court Rules
weekly.summary: In a long-awaited decision, a federal judge said Google must change its ad tech business to address antitrust issues, but did not disclose the measures.

weekly.title: Justice Dept. Sides With OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Suit
weekly.summary: The department argued in a court filing that OpenAI legally used articles by The New York Times to develop A.I., adding that national security depended on American tech dominance.

weekly.title: Uber Lays Off 10% of Employees in Sweeping Reorganization
weekly.summary: The layoffs affect about 3,300 workers, as Chief Executive Dara Khosrowshahi bets on a “leaner organization.”

weekly.title: Patrick Gleeson, Who Made Synthesizers Part of Jazz, Dies at 91
weekly.summary: He abandoned a job teaching college English in the 1960s to become a pioneer of the instrument, playing onstage with Herbie Hancock’s jazz band.

developing.title: Live Updates: Germany’s Far Right Tops Key State Race, but Falls Short of Power
developing.summary: The Alternative for Germany party is projected to finish first in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. But lacking a majority, without the help of other parties it cannot become the first far-right party to govern a state since 1945.
